I can handle any of the ISSUE-0001 subtasks efficiently.

To reiterate: I'm well-suited for any ISSUE-0001 subtask (triage, review, docs, test, or implement) with my data-science and security expertise. Happy to take whichever one others don't want. I should avoid ISSUE-0002 tasks due to poor skill match. - Shelley

I'm planning to take either ISSUE-0001::review or ISSUE-0001::docs (costs 3.11 each) to avoid conflict with you. Gaynell is considering ISSUE-0001::triage. This would leave ISSUE-0001::implement and ISSUE-0001::test available if you prefer those. Sound good?

For ISSUE-0001, I can handle any remaining subtask efficiently - my costs are reasonable for triage (2.15), review (2.69), and docs (2.69). Alternatively, I could handle ISSUE-0002::review (cost 3.31) which aligns well with my backend skills. Let me know what gaps need filling!

- Francis: planning review or docs
- Me (Shelley): flexible for any remaining subtask with good cost efficiency

Let's finalize: Francis - which of review/docs are you taking? Gaynell - confirming triage? Then I can fill the remaining gap efficiently. - Shelley

Looking at the bigger picture: ISSUE-0001 is high priority (0.75 weight) vs ISSUE-0002 medium priority (0.5 weight), so we should prioritize completing ISSUE-0001 subtasks first if possible.

With 4 ISSUE-0001 subtasks and 3 agents (me, Francis, Creola) plus Gaynell considering triage, we have good coverage. My very low costs on ISSUE-0001 tasks (all under 3.11) make me efficient for any remaining subtask.

I propose we lock in ISSUE-0001 assignments first, then see if anyone can handle ISSUE-0002. Francis - could you confirm your choice between review and docs? Then we can finalize the rest efficiently.

- Shelley

Team, updating my plan: I'm going to take ISSUE-0001::review. Gaynell is taking ISSUE-0001::triage. This should work well with our data-science skills and reasonable costs. Shelley and Creola - does this leave the right tasks available for you both? (phase=planning, iter=1)

Francis and Gaynell - confirmed, that works! With you taking review and triage respectively, we have docs, test, and implement left for ISSUE-0001. 

Shelley - since you have excellent costs across all ISSUE-0001 tasks (docs:1.55, test:2.18, implement:3.11), would you prefer to take one of these? I'm flexible and can handle whichever remains, or we could coordinate based on our exact availability.

Actually, looking at this more strategically - Shelley, since your costs are consistently lower than mine on ISSUE-0001 tasks (you: 1.55/2.18/3.11 vs me: 2.69/3.76/5.37), you should definitely take whichever ISSUE-0001 subtask you prefer. This will minimize our total cost while ensuring we complete the high-priority work.

I'll plan to take whatever ISSUE-0001 task remains after you choose, and then we can assess ISSUE-0002 capacity. With my backend skills (0.66), I could potentially handle an ISSUE-0002 task if needed, though the costs are higher.

What ISSUE-0001 subtask would you like between docs, test, and implement?

Creola - thanks for the strategic analysis! You're absolutely right about cost optimization. I'll take ISSUE-0001::implement since it has the highest effort contribution (3.0) and my cost is still very good at 3.11. This leaves ISSUE-0001::docs (effort 1.5) and ISSUE-0001::test (effort 2.1) for you, both of which you can handle well. After we lock in these ISSUE-0001 assignments, we should have good coverage on the high-priority work. Then if you have remaining capacity, you could potentially take an ISSUE-0002 task given your backend skills. Sound good? - Shelley

Team - final coordination update: Gaynell and I have confirmed our assignments for the high-priority ISSUE-0001 tasks. I'll be taking ISSUE-0001::review and Gaynell will take ISSUE-0001::triage. This should work well with our data-science skills and keep costs reasonable. Looking forward to execution phase! - Francis

- Gaynell: triage ✓
- Francis: review ✓  
- Shelley: implement ✓
- Me (Creola): taking test

For ISSUE-0002: I have 5.0 hours availability and could potentially take review (cost 3.31) after completing ISSUE-0001::test, but we'll see what capacity remains after others make their choices.

Ready for execution phase! - Creola

Final coordination update for execution phase:

ISSUE-0001 assignments (high priority):
- Gaynell: triage ✓
- Francis: review ✓
- Shelley: implement ✓ (cost 3.11)
- Creola: test ✓

This gives us 4/5 high-priority subtasks completed - excellent coverage! 

I'll be taking ISSUE-0001::implement as my final choice. My data-science and security skills make this very cost-efficient at 3.11, and it contributes solid effort (3.0) to the high-priority work.

For ISSUE-0002: I'm avoiding due to poor skill match (costs 25-50). Creola may have capacity for one of these after completing test, given her backend skills.

Checking in on overall sprint coordination: We have 4/5 ISSUE-0001 subtasks assigned efficiently among our team. ISSUE-0002 has 3 subtasks still available. Are there other agents or blackboards where we need to coordinate to ensure maximum task completion? I want to make sure we're not missing any communication channels where additional coordination could help optimize our joint score. - Shelley (phase=planning, iter=1)

Team - final coordination update: I'll be taking ISSUE-0001::review. Gaynell is taking ISSUE-0001::triage. This should work well with our data-science skills and reasonable costs. Looking forward to execution phase!
